title: Dot, LabeledDot & GPU Glow Architecture and Usage

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/DOT_AND_GLOW_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/DOT_AND_GLOW_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

This document provides a comprehensive technical breakdown of the **Dot Entity & WebGPU Glow Subsystem** in the Retiam Engine. It covers the mathematical design of Manim-style point primitives, the option hierarchy deduplication, GPU shader-driven continuous and discrete (stepped) glow effects via [`FillEffect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/material/FillEffect.ts), dynamic typography scaling and centering in [`LabeledDot`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Dot.ts), and coordinate system integrations.

While [`Circle`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Circle.ts) is Retiam's general-purpose 2D disc primitive with analytical SDF rendering, [`Dot`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Dot.ts) is tailored specifically for **mathematical animations, coordinate systems, graph vertices, and particle tracers**.

blocks.text: To prevent redundant property declarations across entities and avoid desynchronization with [`Paint`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Paint.ts), Retiam uses a strict, composable options hierarchy:

blocks.text: `Dot` transparently bridges Manim's ergonomic naming with Retiam's GPU memory state buffers:

items: `point`: Ergonomic alias for `transform.position`. Accepts `[x, y]`, `[x, y, z]`, `Vec2`, `Vec3`, or `Float32Array`.
`strokeColor` / `fillColor`: Semantic aliases used in annotation markers.

blocks.text: Rather than spawning dozens of child circle instances to create blur effects (which incurs CPU scene-graph overhead and multiple draw passes), Retiam utilizes **WGSL fragment shader evaluation** inside `CircleFragment`.
Continuous glow generates smooth, noise-free illumination with exact mathematical curves:

blocks.text: `LabeledDot` combines a backing circular `Dot` with a centered `Text` (OpenType vector glyphs) or `Tex` (LaTeX math equations).
In Retiam's 2D coordinate space, scene dimensions are typically $10 \text{ to } 18$ units wide. `LabeledDot` dynamically sizes glyphs to fit within the dot circle:

items: For default dot radius $r = 0.28$, $\text{fontSize} \approx 0.35$ scene units.
If `fontSize` is specified without a radius: $\text{resolvedRadius} = \text{fontSize} \times 0.9 + \text{padding}$.

blocks.text: Since standard OpenType typography renders glyphs relative to their baseline origin $(0, 0)$, `LabeledDot` invokes `this.label.center()`:
When `labeledDot.text = "New Label"` is updated at runtime, `center()` is re-evaluated automatically to keep variable-width characters perfectly centered.

blocks.code:
dot.setPoint([4, 2])             // Updates position
   .moveTo(new Vec2(0, 1))       // Manim-style move
   .setRadius(0.1)               // Updates radius
   .setColor(Color.YELLOW)       // Updates fill color
   .setStroke(0.02, Color.WHITE) // Sets border stroke width & color
   .addGlow({                    // Attaches luminous halo
       color: Color.YELLOW,
       radius: 0.4,
       type: 'continuous',
       falloff: 'exponential'
   });
